- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true prices often rise 1–3 days after model peaks; shift forecast peak forward by 1–3 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.23 → -0.16 → +0.23), model tends to misread momentum; apply a 1–2 day mean-reversion correction to forecast tail.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves unless sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.15) over 3+ days; model underestimates downside risk in such cases.
